questions.problem: Find all the values of $x$ that satisfy $2x-5>1$ or $2x-7<13.$
questions.worked_solution:
We start by solving $2x-5>1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-5 & >1 \\ 2x & >6 \\ x & >3\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237546/assets/2048d360b427cfd94e92a16f7b9f8cd9ca9c88e808bf3b6205d60eebd71aa1cf.png)

Then, we solve $2x-7<13:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-7 & <13 \\ 2x & <20 \\ x & <10\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237546/assets/c1a63d1c991f309dbc10a89f0416c910c2c31bde5fdf069682a6127a1f66987a.png)

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237546/assets/e03d04e5d2d5d571f5b80353081253087f99b2bf58fd86ae56eff3af26415b92.png)

Therefore, the final solution is $x<10$ or $x>3.$ We can write this using interval notation as $x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

questions.problem: Find the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $5x-1>7$ or $2\le 2x+5<16.$
questions.worked_solution:
We start by solving $5x-1>7:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5x-1 & >7 \\ 5x & >8 \\ x & >\frac{8}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237546/assets/0efcf15a3abee964ad2dfc0c1dac12a0f2f43c86180d2ead869fc2ee7b8e9c76.png)

Then, we solve $2\le 2x+5<16:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & \le 2x+5<16 \\ 2-5 & \le 2x<16-5 \\ -3 & \le 2x<11 \\ -\frac{3}{2} & \le x<\frac{11}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237546/assets/22f51dad4248c565cd3afcf03ec9f5a8c50494ad79ed1366b3513083be27182a.png)

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237546/assets/e769eea6e55f7138cbce08cb285253fc1c710c2e39384994a8b36bd43a41ea32.png)

Therefore, the final solution is $x\ge -\frac{3}{2}.$  We can write this using interval notation as $[-\frac{3}{2},\infty ).$

questions.problem: Find all the values of $x$ that satisfy $3x+5>11$ or $2x-3\le 1.$
questions.worked_solution:
We start by solving $3x+5>11:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+5 & >11 \\ 3x & >6 \\ x & >2\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237546/assets/87831ea65f4caa557c8e8826faaa43a60737c3590393872902818921668787d0.png)

Then, we solve $2x-3\le 1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-3 & \le 1 \\ 2x & \le 4 \\ x & \le 2\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237546/assets/4965930532798f18907e5319f2fd9fe5f17d9c1969c12d9795f9867a2cb13351.png)

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237546/assets/a9543d5a2add249d869a667d16bea75780b0e44e4c0d2bde2cf460733d5e9634.png)

Therefore, the final solution is $x\le 2$ or $x>2.$ We can write this using interval notation as

$$
x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

questions.problem: What is the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $6\le 3x+9\le 15$ or $4x-3\ge 5?$
questions.worked_solution:
We start by solving $6\le 3x+9\le 15:$

$$
\begin{aligned}6 & \le 3x+9\le 15 \\ -3 & \le 3x\le 6 \\ -1 & \le x\le 2\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237546/assets/ab1b1f6494c00b463e7912ab3f9710aee553e3a99484822e678494b55268e398.png)

Then, we solve $4x-3\ge 5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-3 & \ge 5 \\ 4x & \ge 8 \\ x & \ge 2\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237546/assets/1b0700462c3957759abbe608c300fece27f92dfdb9b8c14dbeb44cc053de7784.png)

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237546/assets/25f4136a1e248ab30fc0c01feef1e27c331553c1adcf4a1c27c133764cca1ae1.png)

Therefore, the final solution is $x\ge -1.$

questions.problem: Find the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $-8<4x-4<8$ or $2-x>3.$
questions.worked_solution:
We start by solving $-8<4x-4<8:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-8 & <4x-4<8 \\ -4 & <4x<12 \\ -1 & <x<3\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237546/assets/fdf77a12d535974088d36ca7508443a2aab00bb147fde65a17fc06cf5f0bce23.png)

Then, we solve $2-x>3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2-x & >3 \\ -x & >1 \\ \frac{-x}{-1} & <\frac{1}{-1} \\ x & <-1\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237546/assets/8a1af65f2cebbcaeb73c138be5d1cd67d714aacb8db1c995f29b930c06b953fe.png)

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237546/assets/be8cace3271cdfa133d1b647359400681db04f504560ad306e3e1807eb1502d9.png)

Therefore, the final solution is $-1<x<3$ or $x<-1.$ We can write this using interval notation as $(-\infty ,-1)\cup (-1,3).$
